opportunities.title: Keystone Promised to Delete Your Data. It Didn't — And Now Your Address Is Public
opportunities.why_now: A hardware wallet maker's breach exposed exactly the data it told customers would be purged, undercutting the entire pitch of 'cold storage equals safety.'
opportunities.angle: Incident teardown: timeline of the breach, what Keystone claimed vs. what leaked, and why 'we deleted it' is a promise you can never verify

opportunities.title: CoinDCX's CEO Called It a 'False Alarm.' Four Days Later: $16 Million Gone
opportunities.why_now: The gap between the CEO's public denial and the confirmed loss from a retired wallet is a textbook case study in exchange comms failing faster than exchange security.
opportunities.angle: Red-flag timeline piece: denial-to-disclosure gap as a trading signal, with a checklist for spotting the pattern next time

opportunities.title: Initia Halted Its Own Chain to Stop a Mint Exploit — Here's What 'Halting' Actually Means for Your Funds
opportunities.why_now: A live $2.6M mint exploit that forced a chain-wide halt raises the uncomfortable question of who has the keys to pause a 'decentralized' network.
opportunities.angle: Explainer/incident hybrid: how the exploit worked, what powers allowed a halt, and what that says about the chain's actual trust assumptions

opportunities.title: That 'Speed Up This Transaction' Button Was Stealing Your Bitcoin
opportunities.why_now: A wallet bug let rogue servers hijack funds during RBF fee-bumps — a routine, trusted action turned into an attack vector, which is exactly the kind of quiet UX exploit this audience expects.
opportunities.angle: Technical breakdown for a security-literate audience: what RBF does, how the bug worked, and a quick self-check for affected wallets

opportunities.title: Your Validator's Signing Key Might Be Someone Else's Problem Now: The eMudhra and Cloudflare API Mess
opportunities.why_now: Two same-week disclosures — Consensys flagging eMudhra signing risks and Passport phishing traced to compromised Cloudflare API keys — show the attack surface has moved from your wallet to your vendors' vendors.
opportunities.angle: Supply-chain security roundup: map the dependency chain (signing certs, API keys, phishing) and argue why 'audited' no longer means 'safe'
